title: A Protocol for FRET-Based Live-Cell Imaging in Microglia
author: Socodato, Melo, et al.
materials: DMEM, high glucose, GlutaMAX™ Supplement, pyruvate

steps.title: Prepare low‑passage HMC3 culture
steps.instruction: Start a low‑passage HMC3 microglia culture, seeding 5×10^5 cells (2×10^4 cells/cm²) in a T25 flask with supplemented DMEM (10 % FBS, 1 % Pen/Strep) and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; passage cells when they reach 80‑90 % confluence, never allowing confluence below 40 % or above 95 %, and keep passage number ≤20 (avoid passages ≥40). Plan 2–3 passages per week to maintain material availability.

steps.title: Quantify plasmid DNA quality
steps.instruction: Obtain the plasmid encoding the FRET probe, optionally purify with a plasmid DNA kit, then measure concentration (acceptable >1 µg/µL or <200 ng/µL) and purity, ensuring 260/280 ratios of 1.7‑1.9 and 260/230 ratios of 2.0‑2.2.

steps.title: Prepare JetPrime DNA‑lipid complexes
steps.instruction: For each imaging dish, place 200 µL JetPrime buffer in a 1.5 mL tube, add 900 ng plasmid DNA and vortex briefly, add 1.8 µL JetPrime transfection reagent, vortex 10 s, then incubate the mixture at 22‑25 °C for 10 min (DNA:reagent ratio 1:2).

steps.title: Transfect cells and allow expression
steps.instruction: Aspirate medium from the imaging dish, add 2 mL fresh supplemented medium, then add the entire volume of the DNA‑lipid mixture dropwise; incubate 4 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, replace medium with 2 mL fresh supplemented medium, and incubate an additional 16‑20 h (minimum 12‑15 h) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for probe expression. Do not exceed 1 µg DNA per dish, do not skip the medium change, and do not shorten the expression incubation.

steps.title: Process and analyze FRET time‑lapse images
steps.instruction: Export time‑lapse files with metadata, open them in FIJI, inspect donor and FRET channels for aberrations/photobleaching, then perform background subtraction, masking, ratio calculation, and quantitative ROI analysis as detailed below.

substeps.instruction: Inspect donor and FRET channels for fluorescence aberrations and photobleaching (do not skip).

Subtract background for each channel: draw ROI in cell‑free area, measure fluorescence (shortcut “m”), subtract the measured value via Process → Math → Subtract, adjust brightness/contrast (Image → Adjust → Brightness/Contrast → Auto, do not click Apply), and save donor and FRET images as .tiff.

Create a mask: duplicate the entire FRET stack, apply Auto Local Threshold (Image → Adjust → Auto Local Threshold, 8‑bit required), which automatically converts to a binary image, then save the binary stack as .tiff named “mask”.

Generate masked images: use Process → Image Calculator, select image1 = donor (or FRET), image2 = mask, operation = Multiply, check “Create new window” and “32‑bit float”; rename outputs to “masked DONOR” and “masked FRET” and save as .tiff.
Generate ratio image: Process → Image Calculator, image1 = masked FRET, image2 = masked DONOR, operation = Divide, 32‑bit float, then save.
Convert ratio image to 16‑bit: Image → Type → 16‑bit, rename to “FRET‑DONOR”, save as .tiff.
Apply a gradient LUT and adjust image contrast (Image → Adjust → Brightness/Contrast → Auto).
Draw user‑defined ROIs on cells or structures to be quantified.
Transfer ROI coordinates to the ROI Manager (shortcut “t”).
Extract quantitative values using the ROI Manager’s “Multiple Measure” function.
Copy/paste values to a spreadsheet or save as .csv for further analysis.

Optional – generate intensity‑modulated display (IMD) images: download IMDFret.txt from https://doi.org/10.17632/y6z2zmsx4f.1, install via Plugins → Macros → Install, open donor, FRET and IM images, run the IMDFret plugin, select numerator, denominator, and IM image, adjust max/min ratio (multiples of 2) and intensity, then fine‑tune brightness/contrast if needed.
Alternative background subtraction: Process → Subtract Background with appropriate rolling‑ball radius.
If structures move, register donor and FRET stacks before ratio generation via Plugins → Registration → Register Virtual Stack Slices.

description: Timing: 6–7 days1.Start a culture of low passage HMC3 cells and passage them every time they reach 80%–90% confluency (assessed by visually inspecting cells in an inverted phase-contrast microscope).CRITICAL: Do not use cells from cultures that are under-confluent (below 40%) or overly confluent (above 95%), as this will negatively influence transfection efficiency later on. If these cells are allowed to proliferate beyond confluency, they start growing on top of each other and generate big clumps (Figure 1). Splitting cells in these conditions will lead to low growth and survival, severely decreasing transfection efficiency (in the next step). Note: High passage numbers (from 40 upwards) tend to decrease the efficiency of transfection. We typically start cultures from passages up to 20, which allows for several rounds of expansion and collection before going back to a lower batch number. To facilitate cell recovery after thawing, we initially seed 5×105 cells in a T25 flask (density of 2×104 cells/cm2).Note: Planning for 2–3 passages a week by controlling cells' density or maintaining several plates at different confluencies can ensure material availability.Note: We use supplemented DMEM (plus 10% FBS, 1% Pen/Strep) as a medium, but RPMI also gives good results.Note: We incubate the cells at 37°C in an atmosphere of 5% CO2.2.Obtain and quantify the plasmid DNA encoding the FRET probe of interest.Note: The plasmid used in this protocol was a kind gift from Professor Matsuda (see Key Resources Table). We have used many other probes from Addgene, an open platform for deposition, and sharing ready-to-use plasmids (check https://help.addgene.org for information on ordering).Note: High-quality plasmid DNA increases the efficiency of transfection, so, if available, use a plasmid DNA purification kit (but not mandatory).Note: We have successfully used probes from stocks at high (above 1 μg/μL) and low (below 200 ng/μL) concentration.
